configKeys.effect: Blocks only those movements that actually cross a panel's plate; false makes wall and ceiling panels passable from every side, which lets mobs walk into a panel wall and get stuck against it.

Treats a floor panel (FACING=UP) resting on something solid as walkable ground instead of a wall, fixing passages only one block high, while a floor panel with air below stays as it is so mobs keep crossing free-standing panel bridges.
Lets waterlogged panels and steps count as water for swimming mobs, like vanilla slabs do, where Create blocks them outright.

notes:
PROVEN FACTS / GOTCHAS FOR A DOC WRITER

1) Orientation convention is the load-bearing detail: the 3-pixel plate sits at FACING.getOpposite(), NOT at FACING. So FACING=UP is a FLOOR panel (plate in the lowest pixels), FACING=DOWN is a ceiling panel. PanelGeometry's javadoc (PanelGeometry.java:21-26) states dropping getOpposite() would invert the whole module.

2) Self-disabling safety check: CopycatBlocks.panelFacingIsInverted() (compat/CopycatBlocks.java:112-119) verifies that convention once at resolve time by asking the FACING=UP state for its VoxelShape (via EmptyBlockGetter) and demanding min(Y) < 1e-6 && max(Y) < 0.5. If it does not match, `panel` is set back to null and a WARN is logged (:85-90). IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY: only `panel` is nulled - `step` stays resolved, so the water_pathfinding fix for copycat_step keeps running while every panel-related fix, the waterlogged-panel one included, is silently off.

3) Related risk in the same method: it calls defaultBlockState().setValue(BlockStateProperties.FACING, UP) (:113). Should a future Create version ship copycat_panel without a FACING property, vanilla's StateHolder.setValue contract is to throw rather than return null, so the module would crash instead of disabling itself gracefully. Since ensureResolved() is reached lazily from the hot pathfinding hooks, that would surface inside pathfinding, not at load. Not observed; the throwing behaviour is vanilla's, not verifiable from this repo.

4) `resolved` is set to true BEFORE the isLoaded check and the lookups inside the synchronized block (compat/CopycatBlocks.java:79), so any failure leaves both blocks null and the module permanently inert for that game session (fail-safe, but silent).

5) Resolution is deliberately lazy, not resolve-on-load-complete: the javadoc (:67-70) explains that ModuleManager.loadComplete() only calls back into modules enabled at startup - verified in core/ModuleManager.java:149 (it iterates `enabledModules`) - so a module switched on at runtime would otherwise never see its blocks. CopycatPathfindingModule.onLoadComplete() additionally calls ensureResolved() as a warm-up.

6) Two static gate helpers behave differently when the module instance is null: isActive() returns FALSE, while isDirectionAware()/floorPanelsWalkable()/waterPathfinding() return TRUE (`module == null || ...`). Harmless because every hook also checks isActive(), but it looks like an inconsistency at first glance.

7) WHAT isActive() ACTUALLY GATES (the first fact sheet got this framing wrong): AbstractModule.initialize() assigns modEventBus BEFORE the shouldInitialize() check (core/AbstractModule.java:91-98), and isModuleEnabled() keys off `modEventBus != null` (:168-170, :202-211). So without Create the module skips onInitialize() but isActive() still returns true - it reflects the config switch alone. The real Create guard on all three hooks is CopycatBlocks.panel()/step() being null. Conversely the `enabled` switch does work in both distributions: in the bundle the config is registered (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:134) only after initializeModules (:114), so the pre-load read throws, is caught, and the module is initialized anyway; standalone calls module.initialize() unconditionally (core/StandaloneModuleBootstrap.java:62).

8) What is deliberately NOT changed: floor panels keep Create's "not pathfindable" answer in isPathfindable (that is what makes the cell above walkable, i.e. free-standing panel bridges), and copycat_step keeps false on LAND because that is exactly what SlabBlock does. PathComputationType.AIR is untouched ("no evaluator in 1.21.1 asks for it").

9) Coverage limitation, provable from the mixin targets: the direction-aware half only exists on WalkNodeEvaluator. Axolotls are covered for free because AmphibiousNodeEvaluator extends WalkNodeEvaluator. Pure water mobs (SwimNodeEvaluator) and flying mobs (FlyNodeEvaluator) get only the isPathfindable/water fix, no direction awareness - docs/modules/copycat_pathfinding.md "Known limits" 1+2 states this and gives the reason (no source node in their neighbour check).

10) Further known limits, as claimed in docs/modules/copycat_pathfinding.md:88-102 (vanilla behaviour, not verifiable from this repo alone): config toggles need a PathTypeCache eviction to take effect; jump/fall diagonals are only checked start-to-target; a ceiling panel's cell becomes walkable even though a 2-block-high mob does not quite fit; create:copycat_bars was never blocked and is untouched.

11) Pathfinding is not collision - the plate still physically stops mobs. That is why direction_aware=false is explicitly described as making mobs walk into panel walls and get stuck.

12) Performance-sensitive: BlockStateBaseCopycatMixin injects at HEAD of isPathfindable, which runs for every block of every path calculation plus spawn placement. The hot path is two static getters (each a volatile `resolved` read after the first call) and two reference comparisons, with `step()` short-circuited away when the block is already the panel; without Create both fields are null and nothing else is ever touched.

13) Micro-detail the author called out in a comment (WalkNodeEvaluatorCopycatMixin.java:114-115): vpaFloorPanelWalkable uses plain == comparisons instead of an enum switch, because an enum switch inside a mixin emits a synthetic switch-map inner class that Mixin would have to relocate.

14) The two mixins express the same test differently - BlockStateBaseCopycatMixin:74 checks `FACING.getOpposite() == DOWN`, WalkNodeEvaluatorCopycatMixin:105 checks `FACING != UP`. Equivalent (both single out the floor panel), but easy to misread as two different rules.

15) The floor-panel upgrade only fires on a cell vanilla already returned BLOCKED for, and only when the cell below is NOT one of OPEN/WATER/LAVA/WALKABLE; it then returns WalkNodeEvaluator.checkNeighbourBlocks(context, x, y, z, WALKABLE), i.e. the promoted cell still inherits vanilla's danger scan (fire, damaging neighbours).

16) DOC-vs-CODE CONTRADICTIONS worth fixing while documenting:
   - README.md:93 and README.md:302 still link to docs/copycat_pathfinding.md, but the file now lives at docs/modules/copycat_pathfinding.md (docs reorg staged in the working tree, `git status`: R docs/copycat_pathfinding.md -> docs/modules/copycat_pathfinding.md) - both links are dead. README.md:227 (the Create table, "Module skips initialization") is correct and needs no change.
   - docs/modules/copycat_pathfinding.md:73 lists `debug_logging` with default `false`; in AbstractModuleConfig:62-66 it is an ENUM (DebugLoggingMode) defaulting to AUTO, not a boolean.
   - src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml:80-81 comments the optional `create` dependency as belonging to "arm_target_overlay, item_vault_viewer, end_oxygen backtanks, debug_overlay goggles" - copycat_pathfinding is not mentioned although it rides on the same optional dep.

17) The generated standalone toml (build.gradle renderModuleToml, :507-530) declares NO Create dependency at all - only vpa_core/neoforge/minecraft as required plus `incompatible` on the bundle. vpa_copycat_pathfinding loads without Create and the module simply skips initialization. The build.gradle entry (:413-416) lists the three mixins and has no dataGlobs and no moduleDeps. Both mixin configs (bundle and generated) are "required": false, so a missing target disables rather than crashes.

18) No TODO/FIXME/HACK comments anywhere in the module or its mixins. No dead code found. No lang keys, no assets, no data files, no DeferredRegister, no @SubscribeEvent and no event-bus listener of its own - the only lifecycle hooks are onInitialize() (a log line) and onLoadComplete() (ensureResolved warm-up), which is why `events` is empty.

19) Naming: the module's own displayName is "Copycat Pathfinding" (constructor), while the standalone jar's mods.toml displayName is "Vanilla Plus: Copycat Pathfinding" (build.gradle:413) and the jar/modId is vpa_copycat_pathfinding.
oneLiner: Mobs use a passage whose wall, ceiling or floor is lined with Create Copycat Panels again — walking along and under the 3-pixel plate, standing on a supported floor panel, swimming through a waterlogged one — while a panel standing squarely across the way still stops them.

requiredMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/copycat_pathfinding/CopycatPathfindingModule.java:48-50 - shouldInitialize() returns ModList.get().isLoaded("create"); compat/CopycatBlocks.java:80 leaves both block references null without Create; mixin guards at mixin/copycat_pathfinding/BlockStateBaseCopycatMixin.java:55-59, WalkNodeEvaluatorCopycatMixin.java:99-102 and :128-130; README.md:227 ("Module skips initialization (it fixes Create's copycat panels)"); src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml:82-87 (type="optional"); build.gradle:507-530 (renderModuleToml emits no create dep)
requiredMods.whatItAdds: Everything the module acts on: Create supplies create:copycat_panel and create:copycat_step, whose hardcoded isPathfindable = false this module repairs. Without Create the module is skipped at initialization (only a log line is lost, the config section is still built) and all three hooks fall through on a null block reference, so the jar loads and runs inert. No Create class is ever named - the two blocks are looked up from BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK by name - so the code links and compiles without Create. Note the declaration nuance: the BUNDLE's neoforge.mods.toml declares create as type="optional" (versionRange [6.0,), ordering AFTER, side BOTH), and the generated standalone toml declares no Create dependency at all; "required" here means the module does nothing without it, not that the loader enforces it.

shortDescription: Mobs treat Create copycat panels as the thin plate they are instead of a full wall
